title: Which Spanish tax forms affect crypto: 100, 721, 714, 172 and 173
excerpt: Your income tax return, form 721, Wealth Tax and what exchanges report about you on forms 172 and 173 and under DAC8. Who files each one, deadlines for the 2026-2027 season and the real penalties.

seo.metaTitle: Which Spanish tax forms affect your crypto
seo.metaDescription: Forms 100, 721, 714, 172, 173 and DAC8 for crypto in Spain: who files each one, 2026-2027 deadlines and the real form 721 penalties.

imageAlt: Spanish tax forms that affect crypto: 100, 721, 714, 172 and 173
content:
If you hold crypto, over the course of the year you will come across several Spanish tax forms. Some you file yourself: the income tax return (form 100), form 721 if you have crypto held by custodians outside Spain, and form 714 if you are liable for Wealth Tax. Others are filed about you by the exchanges: forms 172 and 173 and, from 2026, DAC8.

Knowing which ones apply to you is the first part. The second is making sure the figures in all of them match, because the AEAT cross-checks them. If you would rather we take care of it, on [declare your crypto taxes](/en/declare-crypto-taxes-spain) we explain how we work.

## Summary: what each form is

| Form | Who files it | What it reports | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 (income tax) | You | Gains, losses and income for the year | April to late June |
| 721 | You, if you exceed the threshold | Balances held by custodians outside Spain at 31 December | 1 January to 31 March |
| 714 (Wealth Tax) | You, if you are required to | All your assets at 31 December, crypto included | Same period as income tax |
| 172 | Providers based in Spain | Your balances at 31 December | January |
| 173 | Providers based in Spain | Your transactions for the year | January |
| DAC8 | Providers serving customers in the EU | Your transactions, exchanged between countries | From 2026 data |

## Form 100: the income tax return, where you pay

The income tax return is the only one of these forms on which you actually pay tax on your crypto. Everything else is information.

### What you declare

- **Capital gains and losses.** Every sale for euros, every swap of one crypto for another (stablecoins included) and every payment made with crypto. The gain is the difference between what you get and what it cost you, with the cost calculated using the FIFO method for each asset.
- **Income from staking, lending and similar.** The Directorate General for Taxation (DGT) generally treats it as income from movable capital, valued in euros on the day you receive it.
- **Other crypto income**, such as airdrops or rewards, depending on their nature.
- **Business income**, if what you do is a business activity, such as [crypto mining](/en/blog/mineria-criptomonedas-fiscalidad-espana) carried out in an organised way.

Gains from sales and swaps are taxed in the savings base, at rates from 19% to 30%. Losses are offset against gains from the same year and, if any are left over, during the following four years. We explain it in detail in [how to offset crypto losses](/en/blog/perdidas-criptomonedas-compensar-declaracion).

### When you have to file

If you have capital gains not subject to withholding, such as crypto gains, and together with other income of that kind they exceed €1,000 a year, you have to file. You also have to file if you have capital losses of €500 or more. In practice, almost anyone who sold or swapped crypto during the year has to file an income tax return.

### Deadline

The filing season runs from early April to late June of the following year. The 2025 return was filed between 8 April and 30 June 2026. The 2026 return will be filed in spring 2027, on the dates set by the AEAT.

## Form 721: crypto held by custodians outside Spain

Form 721 is an information return: you pay nothing for filing it. It lets the tax agency know which crypto you hold through custodians located abroad.

### Who files it

You file it if, at 31 December, the combined balance of your crypto held by custodians outside Spain exceeds **€50,000**. Once you have filed it, you only need to file again if the balance increases by more than €20,000 compared with your last return, or if you stop owning what you declared.

Two details that cause a lot of mistakes:

- **Only what a third party holds for you counts.** What you keep in a self-custody wallet (MetaMask, Ledger, Trust Wallet) does not go on form 721, because the keys are yours and there is no custodian abroad.
- **What matters is where the custodian is**, not where the parent company is. An exchange with an entity registered in Spain reports through form 172, not through your form 721.

### Deadline and penalties

It is filed from 1 January to 31 March of the following year. For balances at 31 December 2026, the deadline ends on 31 March 2027.

The special penalty regime of the old form 720 disappeared after the Court of Justice of the EU ruling of January 2022 and Law 5/2022. Today form 721 follows the **general regime of the General Tax Law**:

- **If you do not file it and the tax agency finds out:** €20 per item or set of data, with a minimum of €300 and a maximum of €20,000.
- **If you file it late on your own initiative, before any request:** half that, i.e. €10 per item of data, with a minimum of €150 and a maximum of €10,000.
- **If you file it with incomplete or false data**, there is a penalty proportional to the amount misreported.

The €10,000 minimum fine per block and the 150% penalty that many websites still repeat no longer exist. Nor did the limitation period disappear: the general four-year period applies.

We prepare it for you in [form 721 filing](/en/form-721-crypto-spain).

## Form 714: Wealth Tax

Form 714 is the **Wealth Tax** return. It is not a declaration of assets abroad (that was the old form 720). It taxes the net wealth you hold at 31 December, and crypto counts as one more asset, wherever it is.

### Who files it

You have to file it if either of these applies:

- **You have tax to pay**, after applying the tax-free allowance and your autonomous community's reliefs.
- **The value of your assets and rights exceeds €2,000,000**, without deducting debts, even if you have nothing to pay.

The general tax-free allowance is €700,000, plus up to €300,000 for your main home. Each autonomous community can change the allowance, the rates and the reliefs, so the result depends a lot on where you live.

Crypto is valued at its market value at 31 December. We go into it in [form 714 and crypto](/en/blog/modelo-714-criptomonedas-patrimonio).

### Deadline

It coincides with the income tax season: April to late June of the following year.

## Forms 172 and 173: what exchanges report about you

Since the 2023 tax year, crypto service providers based or established in Spain file two information returns every January:

- **Form 172:** the balances they hold for each customer at 31 December. Which crypto, how many units and what value.
- **Form 173:** the year's transactions, such as purchases, sales, swaps and transfers, with their dates and amounts. It includes transactions made since 25 April 2023.

You do not have to file anything. What matters is that the tax agency already has this data before you file your income tax return. If you declare sales that do not match form 173, or balances that do not explain what form 172 says, that is where many [tax agency requests](/en/tax-agency-request-crypto) begin.

## DAC8: data exchange in the European Union

The European DAC8 directive has applied since 1 January 2026. It requires crypto-asset service providers operating in the European Union to report their customers' transactions to the tax authority of their own country, which shares the data with each customer's country of residence. The first data, for 2026, will be exchanged in 2027.

In practice, the foreign exchange that used to report nothing to the Spanish tax agency will now do so indirectly. We explain it in [the DAC8 directive and exchanges](/en/blog/directiva-dac8-criptomonedas-exchanges-hacienda).

## Calendar for the 2026-2027 season

| When | What | Who |
|---|---|---|
| January 2027 | Forms 172 and 173 for 2026 | Providers based in Spain |
| 1 January to 31 March 2027 | Form 721 with balances at 31/12/2026 | You, if you exceed the threshold |
| Spring 2027, until late June | 2026 income tax (form 100) and, if applicable, Wealth Tax (form 714) | You |
| 2027 | First DAC8 data exchange | EU tax authorities |

## Mistakes we often see

- **Thinking that switching to a stablecoin is not taxable.** Going from BTC to USDT is a swap, and the gain or loss has to be declared.
- **Including self-custody wallets on form 721**, or leaving out a foreign exchange because "it's just an app".
- **Confusing form 714 with a declaration of assets abroad** and filing it without being required to, or not filing it when your assets exceed €2 million.
- **Filing with the exchange's automatic report.** It does not apply FIFO across your whole portfolio and knows nothing about what you did on other platforms. We cover it in [mistakes when declaring crypto](/en/blog/errores-declarar-criptomonedas).
- **Not keeping your records.** The tax agency can ask about the cost of a sale from four years ago, and the burden of proof is on you.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which form do I have to file if I have only bought crypto?

If you have only bought and have not sold or swapped anything, there is no gain to declare on your income tax return. Even so, you may have to file form 721 if what you hold on foreign exchanges exceeds €50,000 at 31 December, and form 714 if you are liable for Wealth Tax.

### What happens if I did not file form 721 in a year when I should have?

The best thing is to file it as soon as possible, without waiting for the tax agency to ask. Late and without a request, the penalty is €10 per item of data, with a minimum of €150 and a maximum of €10,000. It is worth reviewing that year's income tax return at the same time, so that the declared balance can be explained. We cover it in [regularise your crypto taxes](/en/regularise-crypto-taxes-spain).

### Do I have to declare what I hold on Ledger or MetaMask on form 721?

No. Form 721 only includes crypto held by a custodian located abroad. In a self-custody wallet the keys are yours, so it does not count. It does count for Wealth Tax if you have to file it.

### If the exchange reports to the tax agency with forms 172 and 173, do I still have to declare?

Yes, you still have to declare. Those forms are information for the AEAT, not your return. You still have to calculate the gain or loss on each transaction in your income tax return, and the tax agency will use that data to check that it matches.

### Is form 714 used to declare crypto held abroad?

No. Form 714 is the Wealth Tax and includes all your assets, whether in Spain or abroad. Crypto held by custodians abroad is reported on form 721.
